title: Pool Health & Burst Controls — Compact Thermal-aware Dashboard
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact dashboard panel for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces thermal headroom, oversubscription risk, burst budget, and one-touch autoscale/burst controls. The goal is to let operators make safe burst decisions quickly while understanding cost and SLO trade-offs. This ticket covers wireframes, an interactive Figma prototype, accessibility pass, and a short handoff spec for front-end implementation.
activities: 2025-11-03 - Ticket created after product kickoff; scope constrained to single-pool compact view and burst modal.
2025-11-04 - Baseline metrics and telemetry doc linked from infra: thermal sensors, GPU util percentiles, recent preemptions, per-pool burst credit ledger.
2025-11-05 - First sketch explorations: radial headroom gauge vs. stacked sparkline. Chose stacked sparkline for readability in compact card.
2025-11-06 - Prototype v0 uploaded to Figma. Early feedback from ENG (Kerberos): prefer numeric thresholds and affordances for forced-cooldown state.
2025-11-07 - UX review with PM and Reliability: add explicit 'safe/at-risk' states, color-blind friendly palette, and microcopy explaining thermal hysteresis.
2025-11-08 - Iterate prototype: add predictive oversubscribe warning (ETA to throttle) and cost delta estimator shown when enabling burst.
2025-11-10 - Prepared handoff spec and annotated components for front-end; PR template created for ENG integration work.
2025-11-10 - Accessibility checklist completed: contrast checks, focus order, ARIA labels for burst toggle and modal controls.
reviews: 2025-11-06 - Eng review (Kerberos): 'Prefer explicit cutoff behavior rather than ambiguous colors; add a tooltip explaining KV cache lock during forced cooldown.'
2025-11-07 - PM review (Aisha Rao): 'Tie burst budget to billing estimate and surface amortized cost per 10k tokens so SREs can evaluate impact quickly.'
2025-11-08 - Reliability review (Noah Patel): 'Predictive ETA must degrade gracefully when telemetry is sparse; show confidence bands.'
2025-11-09 - Design critique (team): 'Card should compact to 320px for use in narrow sidebars; burst modal needs a cancelable simulation mode.'
notes: Key UX patterns: 1) 'Headroom' combines thermal and GPU util percentiles to generate a simple safe/at-risk flag. 2) Burst button opens a confirm modal with cost delta and cooldown penalty. 3) Provide read-only compact and expanded detailed views. Implementation should avoid frequent reflows; prefer canvas rendering for sparkline layer.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype includes compact card (320px) and expanded modal with controls.
Annotated spec lists telemetry inputs and fallback when sensor data missing.
Accessibility pass: keyboard operable, ARIA labels, contrast ratio >= 4.5:1 for critical indicators.
Handoff contains CSS tokens, component elevation rules, and interaction states for burst lifecycle (requesting, active, cooldown, failed).
